findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status in UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` callback, but unlike `disconnectMutation` right below it, it has no `onSettled` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. After a user deletes the cache, the `cacheUpdatedAt` value rendered in this same dropdown still comes from the old query data, so the dropdown keeps showing 'Cache Status / Last updated' and the delete option even though the cache rows were just deleted. If the parent doesn't pass an `onChanged` that refetches (it's optional), the stale state persists indefinitely. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` on success/settled for the delete-cache mutation.

findings.title: sed -i '' syntax only works on macOS, script fails on Linux
findings.body: Line 68 uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is the BSD/macOS sed syntax. On GNU sed (Linux), `-i ''` is interpreted as editing a file literally named `''` and the command fails, so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux dev machines or containers. Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm file.bak`) or detect the platform.

findings.title: ENV_FILE relative path breaks depending on invocation directory
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's current working directory, not the script's location. Running the script from the repo root (the natural way: `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) resolves to a `.env` one level above the repo and silently creates/updates the wrong file. Resolve the path from the script's own directory, e.g. `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale, ignoring user's locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so every user sees US-style dates (M/D/YY, 12-hour time) regardless of their configured locale, unlike the rest of the app which formats dates per user preference. Pass the user's locale (available via `useLocale` / i18n language) to `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instead of the hardcoded "en-US".
